why: Flood masks before 2003 have too few observation days (MODIS Aqua launched mid-2002).

decision: Daily flood counts aggregated to the weekly maximum
why: Single days are often cloud-covered; the maximum of the 3-day composites in a week is robust to gaps.
Flood-mask tiles also cover Sudan, Ethiopia and CAR.

decision: Old Lake Victoria / Kyoga files not used after 2002
why: The course files stop in 2002; replaced by NASA G-REALM (1992–2026) in the extended analysis.
evidence_from_data: last Victoria observation in course file: 2002-08-06

decision: Lake levels: weekly median, gaps filled forward only (max 26 weeks)
why: Altimetry passes are irregular; forward filling never uses future values (no look-ahead).
evidence_from_data: Lake Albert: 785 observations, median gap 8 days, longest gap 402 days

decision: Malakal discharge kept only as a local feature, flagged
why: Satellite-derived discharge drops during the biggest floods (saturation artefact).
It lies at 4.9°N 36.0°E in the Omo–Turkana basin, which does not drain to the Nile.

decision: ERA5 hourly accumulations summed to daily totals
why: ERA5 'tp' and 'ro' are hourly accumulations in metres.
evidence_from_data: South Sudan mean rainfall 932 mm/yr (2003–19), plausible

decision: Anomalies relative to the week-of-year climatology of 2003–2019
why: Removes the seasonal cycle; 2003–2019 is the 'normal regime' reference.

decision: Extreme week = unusual area above the 2003–2019 90th percentile
why: Defines 'extreme' relative to the normal regime.

decision: Recurring and unusual pixels counted separately
why: A pixel is classified once per day by the product.
